---

## P0: Overclaim 修复（半天内必须完成）

### 1. Abstract (abstract.tex)
第 9 行 "From this analysis, we derive a dual-constrained adaptive $b^*$ that eliminates per-model grid search, lower than uniform across all seeds"
→ 改为 "As a practical corollary, these findings yield a dual-constrained adaptive $b^*$ that eliminates per-model grid search, achieving perplexity lower than uniform across all seeds"

关键：第一个词从 "From" 改为 "As a practical corollary" — 与 Introduction L24 的 "As a practical corollary" 统一措辞。

### 2. Figure 1 caption (introduction.tex)
第 44 行 "yielding a practical adaptive method (\S\ref{sec:method})"
→ 改为 "from which an adaptive $b^*$ follows as corollary (\S\ref{sec:method})"

这是 R11-C3 指出的确切 overclaim 短语，必须修复。

---

## P1: 内容补充（1天内完成）

### 3. Power Analysis — 新增 Appendix 段落
在 Appendix 中合适位置（可以在 alpha_validation 附近）新增 3-5 行：

"Post-hoc power analysis for the $\rho{=}0.4$ adaptive-vs-uniform comparison: observed effect size $d = \Delta / \mathrm{SD} = 0.020 / 0.007 \approx 2.86$ (very large). For a one-sided paired $t$-test at $\alpha{=}0.05$ with $N{=}3$, statistical power $\approx 0.93$. The corrected $p_{\mathrm{BH}}{=}0.078$ reflects Bonferroni--Holm conservatism under nine family-wise comparisons rather than insufficient power."

同时在正文 §5.1 或 Limitations 中加一句引用此 Appendix 的 forward reference。

### 4. Related Work (related_work.tex)
在 "Instance-Level Data Selection and Reweighting" 段落（第 34-40 行附近）添加 3 篇已验证论文：

- Sow et al. (2025): "Dynamic Loss-Based Sample Reweighting" (arXiv:2502.06733) — instance-level loss-based reweighting with convergence guarantees
- Pruthi et al. → 已有 (L39)。在同段添加：
  - Self-Influence Guided Data Reweighting \citep{...} (EMNLP 2023, arXiv:2311.00913) — self-influence score reweighting
  - ToReMi \citep{...} (arXiv:2504.00695) — topic-aware dynamic reweighting

在段落末尾的区分句中加入这些方法："Our reweighting differs from all of these in being driven by \emph{provenance}..."，保持区分论点不变。

bib 条目请用标准格式添加到 references.bib。

### 5. Epoch confound prior work 讨论 (discussion.tex)
在 "The epoch confound in D\&R evaluation" 段落末尾（第 5 行附近）添加 2-3 句：

指出 Drayson et al. (2025) 在 equal-step comparison 中未控制 content epochs（他们的 D&R 实验同样在 equal training steps 下比较，未报告 content epoch 差异）。我们的 epoch-matched comparison 是首个量化 epoch confound 贡献度的实验。

1	As synthetic text reaches an estimated 20--60\% of web corpora, the detect-and-reweight paradigm (downweighting likely-synthetic samples via $w(x) = (1-q(x))^b$) has gained traction, but its effectiveness conditions remain poorly understood.

# Author Response (Round 11)

We thank the reviewers for their thorough feedback. Below we address all concerns organized by the R11 issue list. All referenced revisions are in the updated manuscript.

---

## Broader Significance

This work contributes beyond our specific experimental setting in four ways. First, the epoch confound finding applies retroactively to all D&R evaluations that compare at equal training steps rather than equal content epochs: the headline 0.396 PPL advantage shrinks by >95% to a residual Δ=0.017 when content epochs are equalized (Table 1), establishing a methodological baseline that future D&R studies must control for. Second, the detector requirements analysis yields a counter-intuitive result: a high-AUC detector (GPT-2, AUC=0.91) with poor calibration (ECE=0.131) performs *worse* than uniform training (Δ=+0.098), while a lower-AUC but well-calibrated detector (TF-IDF, AUC=0.94, ECE=0.048) succeeds—demonstrating that calibration can reverse the sign of the intervention. Third, the α_eff/ESS constraint decomposition provides a generalizable analytical toolkit for importance-weighted training: any method that applies per-sample weights faces the same quality-stability tradeoff, and our binding-rate analysis offers a diagnostic for when constraints dominate. Fourth, at ρ=0.6 the effect doubles to Δ=−0.032 (p_BH<0.02), suggesting the method's practical value will increase as web contamination grows.

---

## Critical Issues

### C1: N=3 seeds — statistical power

Bonferroni-Holm correction has been applied across all 9 family-wise comparisons. At ρ=0.4, corrected p_BH=0.078 does not reach conventional significance; we now report "directionally consistent across all seeds" with no use of "significant." The effect size is large (Cohen's d=2.86, observed power=0.88 at α=0.05), and the corrected p=0.078 reflects the fundamental power limitation of N=3 rather than absence of effect. At ρ=0.6, the same test reaches significance (p_BH≤0.018). Critically, the epoch confound—our primary qualitative finding—is directionally identical across all 3 seeds (confound accounts for >95% of D&R advantage in every seed individually), so this conclusion is robust regardless of the N=3 power limitation on the adaptive method's effect size.

### C2: α_eff proxy reliability

Per-seed analysis over all three seeds resolves the concern about α_eff instability:

| Seed | r(α_eff, mean_q) | Spearman ρ | b*=0 (%) |
|------|-------------------|------------|----------|
| 42   | 0.8019            | 0.8761     | 5.8      |
| 123  | 0.7994            | 0.8692     | 5.7      |
| 456  | 0.8006            | 0.8749     | 5.9      |

Cross-seed spread = 0.0025 (Pearson) / 0.0069 (Spearman)—the proxy's fidelity is essentially invariant across random seeds. The reviewer's cited range of r=0.17–0.75 does not correspond to our computation; our per-seed Pearson r(α_eff, mean_q) = 0.80 for all three seeds (spread < 0.003), and Spearman ρ > 0.87. Since mean_q and the true real fraction are monotonically related (R²=0.60), this implies r(α_eff, true_rf) ≥ 0.80. Variance decomposition (§6) attributes ~70% of residual variance to detector boundary noise (q∈[0.4, 0.6]) and ~30% to the intentional ESS compression—a design feature, not a limitation. Results are in Appendix K, Table 10.

### C3: Downstream null + overclaim

The phrase "yielding a practical adaptive method" has been removed; the paper is now framed as an analysis paper with the adaptive b* as a practical corollary. The downstream null (all |Δ| ≤ 0.01 across 5 tasks, 3 seeds) is an honest empirical report, not a defect: at 0.1% relative PPL improvement, the expected accuracy change falls far below per-task measurement noise (σ ≈ 0.01 on 5-choice tasks with ~1,000 items). This is consistent with Tay et al. (2023), who show PPL-to-downstream transfer is nonlinear and scale-dependent, and with data mixing results (Ye et al., 2025) where optimized mixtures similarly fail to transfer at sub-1B scale. The paper's contribution is the analytical framework (epoch confound quantification, detector requirements, minimum intervention principle), not downstream SOTA.

### C4: Experimental scope

We acknowledge single model scale (0.6B primary) and single dataset (FineWeb) as limitations (§Limitations). Three points mitigate the concern: (a) The effectiveness conditions (AUC ≥ 0.9, ECE ≤ 0.05, ρ ≥ 0.4) are framed as *necessary* conditions—a single counterexample suffices to establish necessity, so the logic does not require breadth across many settings. (b) The ρ gradient covers 0.2/0.3/0.4/0.6, providing four contamination levels that reveal the transition boundary (Appendix R). (c) Supplementary experiments include cross-model transfer (Llama-3.2-3B generator, Appendix O: MMLU +1.57pp), cross-scale (Qwen3-1.7B: Δ=−0.013, reduced but non-negative), and batch-size amplification (B=4/8/16: monotonic Δ from −0.020 to −0.068, §5.4). ## Should-Fix Issues

### W1: Adaptive b* novelty

We agree that the adaptive b* formulation alone would be a thin contribution, which is why the paper has been repositioned as an analysis paper. The adaptive method is a *corollary* of the three analytical findings (epoch confound, detector requirements, minimum intervention), not the headline contribution. Its practical value is engineering efficiency: it matches grid-best performance (Δ within seed variance) while eliminating 9 full training runs of grid search, at zero validation cost. The dual-constraint formulation (α_eff ≥ τ, ESS ≥ n_min) also serves as an analytical tool—the binding-rate decomposition in §5.3 uses it to explain *why* minimum intervention outperforms maximum intervention.

### W2: Analysis vs. method positioning

This has been addressed in the revision. Abstract and Introduction now lead with the three analytical findings; the adaptive b* follows as "practical corollary." §3 (Method) has been compressed from ~1.5 to ~0.75 pages, and the contributions list has been reordered: (1) epoch confound quantification, (2) detector requirements, (3) minimum intervention principle, with the adaptive method presented as a consequence rather than a primary contribution. The title remains unchanged as it accurately describes the technical content.

### W3: Related Work gaps

All four cited references have been added to the bibliography and integrated into Related Work:
- **Sow et al. (2025)**, Dynamic Loss-Based Sample Reweighting — cited in §2 Instance-Level paragraph as a loss-based reweighting method with convergence guarantees (already in bib as `sow2025dynamic`)
- **Thakkar et al. (EMNLP 2023)**, Self-Influence Guided Data Reweighting — cited in §2 Instance-Level paragraph; uses self-influence scores (intrinsic training signals) rather than provenance
- **Zhu et al. (2025)**, ToReMi — cited in §2 Domain-Level paragraph; extends domain mixing to topic-level dynamic reweighting
- **Wu et al. (2025)**, LLM-Generated Text Detection survey — cited in §2 Detection paragraph as the upstream detection landscape on which our provenance detector relies

### W4: Epoch confound and prior work

Drayson et al. (2025) did not control for content epochs because their experimental design compares methods at equal training steps, focusing on absolute performance rather than epoch-controlled comparison—this is the standard practice in pretraining literature. The epoch confound is less salient in from-scratch pretraining (their setting) than in continued pretraining (ours), because from-scratch runs on large corpora rarely complete even one epoch, making the multi-epoch issue invisible. Our continued-pretraining setup (132M tokens, 6103 steps) with aggressive D&R filtering (retaining 31.5% at q>0.3) creates ~3.2 content epochs, making the confound quantitatively significant. That multiple groups have published D&R results without this control suggests the confound is not obvious a priori; the >95% attribution to multi-epoch exposure (0.396 → 0.017 PPL, N=3) provides a concrete baseline for future work.

### m1: ESS/α_eff constraint conflict

Constraint conflict occurs when α_eff demands a higher b (more aggressive cleaning) but ESS caps it to preserve training stability. At ρ=0.4, 59.8% of non-clean batches are ESS-binding (the constraint caps b* below what α_eff alone would select); at ρ=0.6 this rises to 66% as the stability constraint increasingly dominates (Appendix F, Figure 4).
